eligibility.exact_action_basis: The whole House text would require sellers and resale exchanges to display total ticket price when a price is displayed in advertising, disclose it from the first ticket display throughout purchase, and itemize base price and each required fee before purchase completion. Required ticket fees include taxes and listed processing/delivery/facility charges; optional products/services unnecessary to use or possess the ticket are excluded. It prohibits selling/offering/advertising a ticket without actual OR constructive possession, but permits a separate ticket-obtaining service by secondary issuers/exchanges if clearly identified as a service, distinctly separated throughout purchase and disclosed before selection as not guaranteeing a ticket. Resale status must be disclosed before purchase. Affiliation/endorsement claims require an executed partnership agreement OR express written consent; venue names, including misspellings, in secondary sellers/exchanges domain names or subdomains require venue-owner authorization. Cancellation/postponement provisions have an express beyond-reasonable-control exception. They require full total-price refunds for covered cancellation; subject to availability, same/comparable replacement tickets for postponements of no more than six months when originals are invalid; and for postponements over six months a purchaser option between full refund and a qualifying replacement when the original is invalid. Guarantee/refund policy, fee-refund circumstances and how to obtain refunds must be disclosed. Sections2/3/5 expressly use180 days after enactment; no180-day timing is supplied to section4, which lacks that wording. FTC must report within six months on BOTS Act enforcement, coordination/challenges and recommendations. Violations receive section18(a)(1)(B) rule-violation treatment; FTC enforcement, statutory privileges/immunities and other authority are preserved literally without calculating a penalty. The event definition requires a live activity at a venue EXCEEDING200 capacity, public access AND the specified interstate-commerce relationship. Incorporated BOTS definitions include physical/electronic/other ticket evidence, future-event purchase entitlements and several ticket-issuer types; the dated BOTS statute has anti-circumvention/resale predicates and enforcement/security-research exceptions, not a universal software ban. Full FTC Act enforcement and current-law integration are unclaimed. The bill does not show actual seller misconduct, ban all resale or guarantee refunds for every cancellation.

The whole House text would add a calendar-year annual Congress report by the Director of the Office of Credit Risk Management, IN ADDITION TO the existing section657t(h)(2) portfolio report. It covers numbers/types of loan agents assisting7(a) applicants, fraudulent loans involving agent services, the Administrator loan-purchase rate for such loans, referral-fee counts/aggregate value disaggregated by applicant versus lender payer, interest-rate analysis and agency communications. The agent-risk analysis is consolidated WITHOUT naming individual agents and concerns agents meeting the printed not-less-than1-percent dollar-value AND loan-number thresholds, not all agents or either threshold alone. Covered agent services include application help/business-plan/cash-flow/financial documents OR consulting, broker or referral services for a7(a) loan, on behalf of lender or applicant. The dated657t baseline distinguishes Office/Director lender supervision, conditional enforcement and appeals, a separate annual portfolio risk report and an indexed budget submission; the added report neither replaces those duties nor creates a new penalty or guarantee appropriation. Complete636(a) loan-program terms and current implementation are not integrated. No actual fraudulent loan/agent, individual risk finding, construction/technology allocation or improved program performance follows from the reporting requirement.

The whole House text would add ongoing Administrator stakeholder outreach, engagement, education, technical assistance and support BEFORE, DURING AND AFTER Urban Area Security Initiative and State Homeland Security Grant Program awards. Both added subsections include annual State/local/Tribal/territorial stakeholder-feedback surveys, summaries of those surveys and other feedback and how feedback was incorporated in subsequent funding-opportunity notices, plus other feedback mechanisms the Administrator determines appropriate. Within two years after enactment, GAO must report on FEMA outreach/support effectiveness to FEMA and the two named homeland-security committees; within three years, FEMA must report to those committees on actions under the added subsections, including the surveys and summaries. These are added outreach/feedback/reporting duties, not an appropriation, a grant-eligibility expansion or a mandate to build an IT/engineering system. The three attempted604/605/609 baseline locators redirected and are closed without retries; complete underlying program/allowable-use and prior outreach baselines remain unintegrated. The choice therefore supports its own outreach mechanism, not a claim about the whole grants population or first-ever assistance. Preparedness, project-funding and infrastructure outcomes are unclaimed.

The whole House text would direct the SBA Chief Counsel for Advocacy, within180 days after enactment, to establish, operate and maintain a notification hotline concerning compliance burdens reported by a small entity about applicable agency rules, guidance, policy statements or other activity. The Chief Counsel must establish an email address, submission form, phone number OR another appropriate method, and an easily accessible website providing that method; the text does not require every submission channel or specify a vendor/technical system. Starting within one year after enactment of the subsection and annually thereafter, reports to the SBA Administrator and Congress must identify most frequently notified matters/sectors; summarize notifications, submitter type and geography/industry; identify issuing agencies/matters; recommend burden reductions; and summarize Chief Counsel actions/comments/analysis. The report mentions small entities OR other organizations; this does not independently expand who is entitled to use the hotline. The dated634c baseline already supplies complaint/counseling/proposal functions and separate trade outreach/reporting. Incorporated551 agency exclusions and601 rule/small-entity definitions remain material: small entity includes qualified small businesses, nonprofits and small governmental jurisdictions, with statutory qualifications and agency-definition options, not all organizations. Section601 rule has notice-rulemaking predicates and particular-applicability exclusions; it is not every communication called a rule. Printed applicable-to-such-concern wording is retained without redefining small entity. Notifications are reports, not verified burdens, and the bill supplies no automatic agency response, resolution, repeal, savings or actual adverse finding.

The whole as-amended House text would PERMIT State/local/Tribal enforcement agencies and grantees already receiving the four defined categories of eligible Federal funds to use those funds for elder financial fraud, pig-butchering and general-financial-fraud investigations. Optional uses include personnel, specified training, software/technical tools, data/reporting, institution-agency coordination/tabletops and a financial-sector liaison; it does not require every use or appropriate new funds. The February2024 Critical and Emerging Technology List is named in two training clauses, not a blanket condition on all software/personnel uses; its contents are unintegrated. The literal fund definition names TitleIV of the2008PRO-IP Act(30103etseq),28CFRpart23,1401VAWA2022(30107) funds TO A LOCAL law-enforcement agency, and1701 titleI/10381 relating to the described technology/equipment program. The printed section1701 titleI wording and program nicknames are not repaired. Dated30103–30106 evidence includes specific IP-crime grants, a50-percent Federal-share cap and2009–2013 authorizations, federal staffing/tools and reporting; it does not certify present balances or fully reconstruct TitleIV amendments to30101. Dated30107 has conditional appropriations, application/nonsupplanting/coordination and individual-cybercrime predicates, use/reporting limits and2023–2027 authorization, not a universal commercial-fraud grant. Dated10381(a)/(b) supplies mixed policing/technology purposes; remaining current grant law is unintegrated. Part23 is criminal-intelligence operating/privacy/funding policy, including suspicion, relevance, need/right-to-know, safeguards, review and conditional waiver requirements; the bill labels it a grant category but this packet does not adjudicate which actual funds qualify or grant a privacy waiver. Each recipient USING funds for section3(a) purposes must report within one year AFTER THAT USE on amount/purpose, jurisdictional fraud statistics, effects analysis and deterrence assessment; such requested analysis is not proof of causation. Treasury through FinCEN, with the named consultations, must report within one year after enactment on efforts/efficacy/recommendations. The separate state-of-scams report is due within two years and uses the literal and two years thereafter wording without inventing a perpetual every-two-years cadence. It concerns available/suspected BSA reports, aggregate amounts, typologies/digital assets and Rapid Response referrals, sums sought for interdiction VERSUS sums actually interdicted/recovered and referral-related limits; suspected reports and aggregates are not adjudicated fraud or proven victim losses. Fund-providing agencies must report annually to four committees with recipient reports. Federal agencies MAY assist State/local/Tribal agencies and fusion centers using blockchain/related tracing tools; mandatory assistance, unrestricted surveillance, actual recovery, implementation and current grant eligibility are unclaimed.

source_render_constraints.detail: Five held episodes pending independent preparation review and separate meaning/eligibility decisions. General reporting/outreach versus direct technology relationships and literal grant/program baselines stay qualified; zero propositions.
